headline: Veteran actor Nana Patekar dies at 75 after cardiac arrest
summary: The acclaimed Indian filmmaker and actor, known for his intense performances and social activism, passed away at his residence in Goa.
details: Veteran Indian actor and filmmaker Nana Patekar has died after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. He was 75 years old.
According to hospital sources, Patekar was found unconscious at home and brought to the hospital, where doctors tried to revive him for nearly 45 minutes before he was declared dead at 5:20 AM.
Born Vishwanath Patekar on January 1, 1951, in Maharashtra, he became one of Indian cinema's most acclaimed actors, known for his distinctive dialogue delivery and complex characters.
A three-time National Film Award winner, his notable films include 'Natsamrat', 'Wajood', 'Parinda', 'Ab Tak Chhappan', and 'Yeshwant'.
He earned widespread praise for roles in 'Shakti: The Power', 'Apaharan', 'Taxi No 9211', and his comedic turn as gangster Uday Shetty in 'Welcome' and 'Welcome Back'.
In 2016, he won the Filmfare Award for Best Actor for the Marathi film 'Natsamrat', and he was awarded the Padma Shri in 2013 for his contributions to the arts.
Beyond acting, Patekar was a playback singer and was deeply involved in social causes, particularly supporting farmers and families affected by agrarian distress.
His son, Malhar Patekar, who was in Pune at the time of the incident, has since traveled to Goa.
caption:
Indian cinema loses a legend. Veteran actor Nana Patekar has passed away at 75.

Veteran Indian actor and filmmaker Nana Patekar has died after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. He was 75 years old.

According to hospital sources, Patekar was found unconscious at home and brought to the hospital, where doctors tried to revive him for nearly 45 minutes before he was declared dead at 5:20 AM.

Born Vishwanath Patekar on January 1, 1951, in Maharashtra, he became one of Indian cinema's most acclaimed actors, known for his distinctive dialogue delivery and complex characters.

A three-time National Film Award winner, his notable films include 'Natsamrat', 'Wajood', 'Parinda', 'Ab Tak Chhappan', and 'Yeshwant'.

He earned widespread praise for roles in 'Shakti: The Power', 'Apaharan', 'Taxi No 9211', and his comedic turn as gangster Uday Shetty in 'Welcome' and 'Welcome Back'.

In 2016, he won the Filmfare Award for Best Actor for the Marathi film 'Natsamrat', and he was awarded the Padma Shri in 2013 for his contributions to the arts.

Beyond acting, Patekar was a playback singer and was deeply involved in social causes, particularly supporting farmers and families affected by agrarian distress.

His son, Malhar Patekar, who was in Pune at the time of the incident, has since traveled to Goa.

headline_marked: 4 workers burnt in [[furnace blast at Rupganj steel mill]]
headline: 4 workers burnt in furnace blast at Rupganj steel mill
summary: The accident occurred at Premier Steel Re-Rolling Mills (PSRM) on Wednesday evening, leaving several workers injured.
details: Four workers were burnt in a blast at Premier Steel Re-Rolling Mills (PSRM) in Narayanganj's Rupganj on Wednesday evening.
The accident happened around 8pm in the Barpa Ariabo area of Tarabo municipality. It is believed that a leak in the furnace caused molten iron to spill out, leading to the explosion.
The injured workers were identified as Sajib Sarkar (32), Rubel Ahmed (28), Nazmul (33), and Abir (19).

According to Sultan Mahmud Shikder, a resident physician at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, Sajib suffered burns to 70 percent of his body, while Rubel, Nazmul, and Abir suffered burns of 25, 20, and 10 percent respectively.
A colleague, Nabil Talukdar, reported hearing screams and seeing sparks of fire spreading after the furnace exploded shortly after he had left the mill.
caption:

According to Sultan Mahmud Shikder, a resident physician at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, Sajib suffered burns to 70 percent of his body, while Rubel, Nazmul, and Abir suffered burns of 25, 20, and 10 percent respectively.
